You are given a permutation P = (P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_N) of (1, 2, \ldots, N). Takahashi can repeatedly perform the following operation on P (possibly zero times):
- Choose an integer i satisfying 1 \leq i \leq N-1. Pay a cost of i, and swap P_i and P_{i+1}.
Find the minimum total cost required to sort P in order. Yes. The goal is to sort P in ascending order so that P_1 < P_2 < \ldots < P_N.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N
P_1 P_2 \ldots P_N
Output
Print the minimum total cost required to sort P in order.
Constraints
- 2 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5
- (P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_P) is a permutation of (1, 2, \ldots, N).
- All input values are integers.
